brief: The Fed hiked 25 basis points to a 3.75-4% target range. Fed Chair Warsh called it removing a dose of accommodation and said conditions were not restrictive. The Fed's Summary of Economic Projections showed stickier inflation and stronger growth expectations, a dot plot median of 4.1% for 2026 implying another hike, and eight participants seeing a third hike in 2027. Broad policymaker support for more hikes led markets to price three further hikes by mid-2027. UBS keeps its December-hike call but calls that pricing excessive, though it flags upside risk, reads the median dot as a 2027 hold, and forecasts steady disinflation over six months as base effects weaken the case for a long hike sequence. So UBS keeps fixed income Attractive: add duration selectively in high-quality bonds, take investment-grade carry at medium tenors, keep high-yield and emerging-market credit short-dated, but avoid the longest maturities since fiscal strain, AI-related debt issuance and price-sensitive buyers should keep term premiums elevated. Separately, UK CPI rose to 3.1% in August with core inflation steady at 2.6%, yet UBS expects the BoE to hold at 3.75% through 2026, arguing hike odds are overstated though energy-driven risk could delay cuts. UBS rates GBP Attractive.
